analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | after the bell ... (Ryan Novak, 28 Oct 2026)
key_insights: FOMC held the fed funds target range at 3.75-4.00% at its October meeting after a 25bp hike in September. Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp increase.

The FOMC statement kept the language that inflation 'remains elevated' and upgraded its description of economic activity to 'expanding at a strong pace' from 'solid'. The rest of the statement was unchanged from September.

FDX reported an EPS beat of $3.74 on revenue of $22.9bn and raised full-year EPS guidance to $18-18.60 from $16.90-18.10. Full-year revenue growth is now seen at 12% vs 11% prior. The desk calls it a big guide raise, with a new CFO likely to update on the balance sheet.

STRL reported Q3 EPS of $7.58 vs $6.17 consensus on revenue of $1.56bn vs $1.19bn consensus, and raised full-year guidance (revenue $4.63-4.73bn vs $4-4.15bn prior). The desk's read is mixed: guidance implies weaker margins, but 70% organic growth is hard to ignore.

HONA beat on Q3 EPS ($2.21 vs $1.87) and revenue ($4.64bn vs $4.56bn), with backlog up 12% to $19.32bn. Full-year revenue growth guidance of 4-5% is unchanged and EBIT of $4.375-4.425bn was narrowed. The desk reports mixed feedback because of a $50mm net IEEPA benefit in the quarter and an underwhelming core guide after a big run.

ARXS beat on Q3 EPS ($0.37 vs $0.20), sales ($564mm vs $541mm) and EBITDA ($256mm vs $220mm). It raised full-year EBITDA to $855-865mm vs $790-800mm prior and introduced 2027 guidance. The desk notes the bar is high because it has been one of the few SMID A&D names that has performed well.

AMRZ Q3 EBITDA of $1.08bn was in line with consensus, but revenue of $3.77bn missed $3.85bn and full-year EBITDA ($2.95-3.05bn) and revenue ($12.2-12.4bn) guidance was cut. The desk says feedback is cautious and the stock sits on its 50-day average after a big move in recent weeks.

F beat on Q3 EPS ($0.49 vs $0.41) and EBIT ($2.66bn vs $2.37bn consensus), and sees full-year EBITDA at the high end of $10.5-11bn. The desk says it stands out positively given weak auto prints across the board.
MYRG beat on Q3 EBITDA ($110mm vs $89mm), contract revenue ($1.26bn vs $1.16bn) and EPS ($3.82 vs $2.97). Backlog rose to $3.68bn and the board approved a new $100mm repurchase program.
MTH missed on Q3 EPS ($1.11 vs $1.17) and revenue ($1.17bn vs $1.29bn). Orders fell 15% y/y and gross margin was 17.4% vs 18% consensus. The desk describes the results as weak across the board.
CSL beat on EPS ($5.92 vs $5.89) and revenue ($1.5bn vs $1.42bn) but missed on EBITDA ($348mm vs $352mm). The desk finds the Q4 guide underwhelming, with margins down on 9% organic growth.

MGRC Q3 EBITDA ($107mm vs $102mm) and EPS ($2.00 vs $1.89) beat. Full-year revenue guidance was lowered to $945-960mm from $955-985mm and gross rental capex was raised to $270-290mm from $200-220mm. The desk says the capex increase will pressure cash.

CP reported Q3 EPS of $1.28 vs $1.30 on revenue of $4.22bn vs $4.21bn, in line. The desk says numbers are hard to beat here, though fundamentals favor US rails. Fuel is a headwind to the operating ratio.
CVNA Q3 EBITDA was $800mm vs $791mm on revenue of $8.04bn vs $7.71bn, with retail GPPU down 5%. The desk sees a lowered bar and expects the Q4 commentary to be well received.

FLS beat on Q3 EPS ($1.07 vs $0.98) with in-line revenue of $1.24bn, bookings of $1.38bn (+12% y/y) and a 1.12x book-to-bill. It raised the low end of full-year EPS guidance to $4.10-4.20. The desk calls it solid with strong bookings, with some concern over Middle East exposure.
EFOR beat on Q3 EPS ($1.11 vs $1.02) and revenue ($1.03bn vs $1.01bn). Q4 EPS guidance of $0.95-1.11 brackets the $1.01 consensus. The desk calls the guide fine.
MSFT, GOOGL and ORCL traded mixed after hours. FDX, FLS, HONA and STRL were the most discussed post-market names.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates were left unchanged after a 25bp hike in September. Two dissents favored another 25bp hike, which points to a hawkish tilt on the committee.

macro_indicators.reading: Two dissents (Cook, Hammack) in favor of a 25bp hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hammack also dissented in favor of a hike in July. Dissent from the hawkish side suggests some members see inflation as not yet contained.

macro_indicators.reading: 'expanding at a strong pace' vs 'solid' previously
macro_indicators.interpretation: The statement upgrade, together with 'inflation remains elevated', leaves little room to signal cuts.

AMRZ price increases are not enough to offset inflation, leaving EBITDA flat y/y, and weather affected Q3.

MGRC's higher rental capex will pressure cash.
FLS carries Middle East exposure concerns.

Hawkish Fed dissents point to the risk of further rate hikes.
